title: Restriction identifies the proper coefficient comparison with the pro-etale projection map
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$; let $\bar X$ and $Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$ and $p:\bar X\to Y$ a proper $k$-morphism [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$. On the small pro-étale sites use the ordinary uncompleted constant-ring module derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},R)$ for $R=A,B$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], the derived adjunctions $p_R^*\dashv Rp_{*,R}$ with counits $\varepsilon^R$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], the constant-ring identifications $p^{-1}R_Y\simeq R_{\bar X}$ [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], and scalar extension $T_T=(-)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_T}B_T$ with its $B_T$-action [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Let $r_T:D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},B)\to D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ be restriction of scalars, so that $r_TT_TK=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_T}B_T$ with $B_T$ regarded as an $A_T$-module, and let $d:r_YRp_{*,B}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{*,A}r_{\bar X}$ be the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. For $N\in D(\bar X_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ let
$$\gamma_N:T_YRp_{*,A}N\longrightarrow Rp_{*,B}T_{\bar X}N$$
be the unique $B$-linear map whose adjoint transpose under $p_B^*\dashv Rp_{*,B}$, after the canonical identification $p_B^*T_Y\simeq T_{\bar X}p_A^*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], is $T_{\bar X}(\varepsilon^A_N)$. Then the $A$-linear map
$$d_{T_{\bar X}N}\circ r_Y(\gamma_N):Rp_{*,A}N\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_Y}B_Y\longrightarrow Rp_{*,A}\bigl(N\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_{\bar X}}B_{\bar X}\bigr)$$
is the pro-étale projection morphism for the coefficient object $B_Y$: its adjoint transpose under $p_A^*\dashv Rp_{*,A}$, composed with the tensor-pullback identification $p_A^*(Rp_{*,A}N\otimes^{\mathbf L}B_Y)\simeq p_A^*Rp_{*,A}N\otimes^{\mathbf L}B_{\bar X}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], is $\varepsilon^A_N\otimes^{\mathbf L}1_{B_{\bar X}}$. This identification is natural in $N$. No boundedness of $N$ and no flatness or finite Tor dimension of $B$ over $A$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $L_R=p_R^*$ and $R_R=Rp_{*,R}$ for $R=A,B$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] with $u=p$, $R_T=A_T$ and $S_T=B_T$. Its coefficient-square hypothesis holds: the identifications $c_A,c_B$ of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] preserve constant sections, so both composites $p^{-1}A_Y\to B_{\bar X}$ send each locally constant $a$ to its image in $B$. They therefore agree as sheaf maps. Denote the supplied inverse-image comparison by $b:r_{\bar X}L_B\simeq L_Ar_Y$ and retain the specified direct-image comparison $d:r_YR_B\simeq R_Ar_{\bar X}$. In particular the cited adjunct identity applies on the ordinary unbounded categories in the statement.

source.place: Step 1, normalization of the proper coefficient map and its etale comparison

proof.text:
Write $\theta_K:L_BT_YK\simeq T_{\bar X}L_AK$ for the coefficient/pullback identification in the definition of $\gamma$. Under $r_TT_TK=K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B_T$ its underlying comparison is
$$r_{\bar X}(\theta_K)\circ b_{T_YK}^{-1}=\tau_K,$$
where $\tau_K:L_A(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B_Y)\simeq L_AK\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B_{\bar X}$ is the tensor-pullback comparison. Here is the normalization check. Identified-coefficient module pullback is inverse image with transported action [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; $b$ forgets the $B$-action in that same inverse image. For an $A_Y$-module complex $P$, the ordinary coefficient/pullback comparison is the balanced map $p^{-1}(P\otimes_A B_Y)\to p^{-1}P\otimes_A B_{\bar X}$ sending an inverse-image pure tensor of $x$ and $s$ to $p^{-1}x\otimes c_B(p^{-1}s)$. Forgetting the action gives exactly the ordinary tensor comparison; the tensor/sheafification definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] makes equality on these local generators equality of sheaf maps. Apply this in every degree to a flat K-flat representative $P$ of $K$. Scalar extension is computed this way by [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]; pullback preserves such representatives by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For the underlying tensor comparison one may also resolve $B_Y$; its augmentation to $B_Y$ gives the same map by the displayed pure-tensor equation and naturality. Localization and inversion of these quasi-isomorphisms preserve the equation, with independence of representatives by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Thus the identity holds for every unbounded $K$.

source.place: Step 1, normalization of the proper coefficient map and its etale comparison

proof.text:
Set $K=R_AN$ and $t_N=T_{\bar X}(\varepsilon^A_N)\circ\theta_{R_AN}:L_BT_YR_AN\to T_{\bar X}N$. By definition its $B$-adjunct is $\gamma_N$. The precise adjunct clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], applied with $M=T_YR_AN$ and target $T_{\bar X}N$, says that the $A$-adjunct of $r_{\bar X}(t_N)\circ b_{T_YR_AN}^{-1}$ is $d_{T_{\bar X}N}\circ r_Y(\gamma_N)$. Expanding $t_N$ and using Step 2 gives
$$r_{\bar X}(t_N)\circ b_{T_YR_AN}^{-1}=(\varepsilon^A_N\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}1_{B_{\bar X}})\circ\tau_{R_AN},$$
since extension sends a morphism $v$ to $v\otimes^{\mathbf L}1_B$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. The adjunction bijection is injective, so the displayed restricted map equals the projection map defined by this transpose. This proves the asserted identity without a projection-formula invertibility claim.

source.place: Step 1, normalization of the proper coefficient map and its etale comparison

proof.text:
For a morphism $v:N\to N'$, counit naturality gives $v\circ\varepsilon^A_N=\varepsilon^A_{N'}\circ L_AR_A(v)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Tensor it with $1_{B_{\bar X}}$ and use the naturality of $\tau$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. If $h_N=(\varepsilon^A_N\otimes^{\mathbf L}1_B)\circ\tau_{R_AN}$, the resulting equation is
$$(v\otimes^{\mathbf L}1_B)\circ h_N=h_{N'}\circ L_A(R_A(v)\otimes^{\mathbf L}1_B).$$
Transpose this equation through $L_A\dashv R_A$; the Hom bijection is natural in both variables by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. It says exactly that the projection maps, and hence the maps identified in Step 3, are natural in $N$. All comparisons above were on the unbounded categories; no step used flatness of $B$ over $A$ or boundedness of $N$.
